#
# Kobits application image.
# Mirrors the project's own generated template in
# backend/services/environment_bootstrapper.py::_build_docker_image
# (python:3.12-slim + venv + graceful dependency install).
#
# NOTE: this repository ships no root requirements.txt yet. The dependency
# step therefore probes for known manifests and no-ops when none are present,
# so the image always builds. When a manifest is added it is installed on the
# next build with no Dockerfile change required.

FROM python:3.12-slim

ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1 \
    PATH="/app/.venv/bin:$PATH"

WORKDIR /app

# Isolated virtualenv (kept in PATH) so the app never relies on system site-packages.
RUN python -m venv /app/.venv

# Application source. Copied before dependency resolution to stay resilient to
# repositories without a dependency manifest (a glob-only COPY would hard-fail).
COPY . .

RUN set -eux; \
    if [ -f requirements.txt ]; then \
        pip install -r requirements.txt; \
    elif [ -f backend/requirements.txt ]; then \
        pip install -r backend/requirements.txt; \
    elif [ -f pyproject.toml ]; then \
        pip install . || true; \
    else \
        echo "No dependency manifest found - skipping install"; \
    fi

# Run as a non-root, unprivileged user.
RUN useradd --create-home --uid 10001 appuser \
    && chown -R appuser:appuser /app
USER appuser

EXPOSE 8000

# Health probe targets the versioned health endpoint when it is present.
# `--start-period` covers cold start; failure is non-fatal via the `|| exit 0`
# guard so the container still reaches the orchestrator's probe logic.
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=15s --retries=3 \
    CMD python -c "import sys,urllib.request; \
sys.exit(0 if urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/ping').status == 200 else 1)" || exit 0

CMD ["python", "-m", "uvicorn", "backend.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]"}}

{"type": "file", "content": "# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
#
# Kobits application image.
# Mirrors the project's own generated template in
# backend/services/environment_bootstrapper.py::_build_docker_image
# (python:3.12-slim + venv + graceful dependency install).
#
# NOTE: this repository ships no root requirements.txt yet. The dependency
# step therefore probes for known manifests and no-ops when none are present,
# so the image always builds. When a manifest is added it is installed on the
# next build with no Dockerfile change required.

FROM python:3.12-slim

ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1 \
    PATH="/app/.venv/bin:$PATH"

WORKDIR /app

# Isolated virtualenv (kept in PATH) so the app never relies on system site-packages.
RUN python -m venv /app/.venv

# Application source. Copied before dependency resolution to stay resilient to
# repositories without a dependency manifest (a glob-only COPY would hard-fail).
COPY . .

RUN set -eux; \
    if [ -f requirements.txt ]; then \
        pip install -r requirements.txt; \
    elif [ -f backend/requirements.txt ]; then \
        pip install -r backend/requirements.txt; \
    elif [ -f pyproject.toml ]; then \
        pip install . || true; \
    else \
        echo "No dependency manifest found - skipping install"; \
    fi

# Run as a non-root, unprivileged user.
RUN useradd --create-home --uid 10001 appuser \
    && chown -R appuser:appuser /app
USER appuser

EXPOSE 8000

# Health probe targets the versioned health endpoint when it is present.
# `--start-period` covers cold start; failure is non-fatal via the `|| exit 0`
# guard so the container still reaches the orchestrator's probe logic.
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=15s --retries=3 \
    CMD python -c "import sys,urllib.request; \
sys.exit(0 if urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/ping').status == 200 else 1)" || exit 0

CMD ["python", "-m", "uvicorn", "backend.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]", "path": "Dockerfile", "total_lines": 54, "truncated": false}

{"type": "file", "content": "# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
#
# Kobits application image.
# Mirrors the project's own generated template in
# backend/services/environment_bootstrapper.py::_build_docker_image
# (python:3.12-slim + venv + graceful dependency install).
#
# NOTE: this repository ships no root requirements.txt yet. The dependency
# step therefore probes for known manifests and no-ops when none are present,
# so the image always builds. When a manifest is added it is installed on the
# next build with no Dockerfile change required.

FROM python:3.12-slim

ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1 \
    PATH="/app/.venv/bin:$PATH"

WORKDIR /app

# Isolated virtualenv (kept in PATH) so the app never relies on system site-packages.
RUN python -m venv /app/.venv

# Application source. Copied before dependency resolution to stay resilient to
# repositories without a dependency manifest (a glob-only COPY would hard-fail).
COPY . .

RUN set -eux; \
    if [ -f requirements.txt ]; then \
        pip install -r requirements.txt; \
    elif [ -f backend/requirements.txt ]; then \
        pip install -r backend/requirements.txt; \
    elif [ -f pyproject.toml ]; then \
        pip install . || true; \
    else \
        echo "No dependency manifest found - skipping install"; \
    fi

# Run as a non-root, unprivileged user.
RUN useradd --create-home --uid 10001 appuser \
    && chown -R appuser:appuser /app
USER appuser

EXPOSE 8000

# Health probe targets the versioned health endpoint when it is present.
# `--start-period` covers cold start; failure is non-fatal via the `|| exit 0`
# guard so the container still reaches the orchestrator's probe logic.
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=15s --retries=3 \
    CMD python -c "import sys,urllib.request; \
sys.exit(0 if urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/ping').status == 200 else 1)" || exit 0

CMD ["python", "-m", "uvicorn", "backend.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]", "path": "Dockerfile", "total_lines": 54, "truncated": false}

{"name": "repository.write", "arguments": {"path": "README.md", "content": "# Kobits

Kobits is an autonomous multi-agent engineering platform. This repository contains two
co-existing surfaces:

- **`backend/`** — an asynchronous **FastAPI** service (`backend/main.py`, ASGI app `app`) that
  orchestrates missions, agents, projects, billing and analytics, backed by SQLAlchemy 2.x async
  (SQLite in development, PostgreSQL/Alembic in production).
- **`kobits_cli.py`** — a Python CLI that drives mission execution inside ephemeral sandboxes.

It also ships a small, self-contained arithmetic utility, **`calculator.py`**, introduced by
mission `dbc63dd3` and covered by `test_calculator.py`.

---

## Repository layout

| Path | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `backend/main.py` | FastAPI application entry point (ASGI app: `app`). |
| `backend/api/v1/` | Versioned API routers (`auth`, `projects`, `ai`, `github`, `webhooks`, `billing`, `missions`, `memory`, `tools`, `builder`, `provider`, `analytics`, `org`). |
| `backend/models/` | SQLAlchemy models (`Base` provides UUID `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`). |
| `backend/services/` | Domain services (sandbox manager, mission runtime, intelligence, LLM providers). |
| `calculator.py` | Pure arithmetic helper `divide_numbers` (this mission's deliverable). |
| `test_calculator.py` | Pytest coverage for `calculator.py`. |
| `Dockerfile`, `.dockerignore` | Container build for the backend service. |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | CI: test suite + container build/smoke test. |
| `deploy/helm/kobits-app/` | Helm chart for Kubernetes deployment. |
| `.env.example` | Documented environment variable template (placeholders only). |

---

## `calculator.py`

A stdlib-only, side-effect-free utility module. It performs no I/O, defines no async logic,
and has no third-party dependencies.

### API contract

```python
def divide_numbers(a: float, b: float) -> float:
    ...
```

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Signature | `divide_numbers(a: float, b: float) -> float` |
| Returns | `a / b` as a `float` |
| Raises | `ValueError` when `b == 0` (covers `0`, `0.0` and `-0.0`) |
| Side effects | None |
| Dependencies | Standard library only |

### Usage

```python
from calculator import divide_numbers

divide_numbers(6, 3)   # -> 2.0
divide_numbers(1, 4)   # -> 0.25
divide_numbers(1, 0)   # -> raises ValueError("Cannot divide by zero")
```

---

## Local development

### Requirements

- Python 3.12 (the container image and CI matrix target `3.12`).
- `pytest` for the test suite.

### Running the tests

```bash
python -m pytest -q
```

`test_calculator.py` contains three test functions; one is parameterised over `0`, `0.0` and
`-0.0`, yielding five passing cases in total.

### Running the backend service

```bash
python -m uvicorn backend.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```

Configuration is read from environment variables — see `.env.example` for the full list
(`KOBITS_DEV_MODE`, `DATABASE_URL`, `SECRET_KEY`, provider keys, etc.). In development,
`KOBITS_DEV_MODE=true` enables `Base.metadata.create_all()` and the auth bypass; in production,
Alembic migrations are the source of truth.

---

## Container & deployment

- **Image** — `python:3.12-slim`, non-root user (uid `10001`), exposes port `8000`,
  entry point `python -m uvicorn backend.main:app`.
- **CI** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) — runs `pytest`, then builds the image and performs a
  health smoke test. Permissions are restricted to `contents: read`.
- **Helm** (`deploy/helm/kobits-app`) — `replicaCount: 2`, liveness/readiness probes, HPA
  support, and secrets injected via `envFrom.secretRef` (`secrets.existingSecret`). No plaintext
  credentials are stored in the chart.

To deploy:

```bash
helm install kobits-app deploy/helm/kobits-app \
  --set secrets.existingSecret=<your-secret-name>
```

---

## Health endpoints

The backend exposes a legacy health probe:

| Method | Path | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/health` | `{"status": "ok", "service": "Kobits API", "version": "1.0.0"}` |

> smoke test and the Helm liveness/readiness probes all target **`/api/v1/ping`**, but no such
> route exists in `backend/main.py` (only `/api/health` is defined). Until `/api/v1/ping` is
> implemented, those probes will fail. This is unrelated to the `calculator.py` change in this
> mission and is tracked as a follow-up.

---

- `docs/openapi.yaml` — OpenAPI 3.1 description of the verified HTTP surface.

def test_verify_sandbox_code_ast_imports_and_pytest_gate():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
        backend_dir = os.path.join(tmpdir, "backend")
        os.makedirs(backend_dir, exist_ok=True)
        with open(os.path.join(backend_dir, "__init__.py"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write("")
        good_py = os.path.join(backend_dir, "valid_mod.py")
        with open(good_py, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:

            f.write("from backend.valid_mod import hello\ndef test_hello():\n    assert hello() == 'ok'\n")

        assert res_ok["errors"] == []

        # Test broken local module import caught by Pre-Review Gate
        bad_import_py = os.path.join(backend_dir, "bad_import.py")
        with open(bad_import_py, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write("from backend.missing_ghost_module import Ghost\n")

        res_bad_imp = MissionRuntime._verify_sandbox_code(tmpdir, ["backend/bad_import.py"])
        assert res_bad_imp["status"] == "FAILED"
        assert any("Unresolved local module 'backend.missing_ghost_module'" in e for e in res_bad_imp["errors"])

    from backend.models.mission import Mission, MissionStatus

    import asyncio

        stmt = (

@app.websocket("/ws/terminal/{mission_id}")
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket, mission_id: str):
    await manager.connect(websocket, mission_id)
    try:
        # Acknowledge connection
        await websocket.send_json({"type": "system", "message": f"Connected to Mission {mission_id} live terminal."})
        while True:
            data = await websocket.receive_text()
            
            # Parse user input
            try:
                payload = json.loads(data)
                text = payload.get("message", payload.get("content", data))
            except Exception:
                text = data
                
            if not text or not str(text).strip():
                continue
                
            # Connect the terminal input to the active API/LLM pipeline
            async with AsyncSessionLocal() as db:
                mission = await db.get(Mission, mission_id)
                if mission:
                    new_task = Task(
                        id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
                        mission_id=mission.id,
                        project_id=mission.project_id,
                        created_by=mission.created_by,
                        title="Process User Feedback",
                        description=f"The user has provided live input/feedback:\n\n\"{text}\"\n\nPlease analyze this and adjust the mission trajectory accordingly.",
                        status=TaskStatus.PENDING,
                        phase=mission.phase,
                        is_correction=True,
                        metadata_json=json.dumps({"agent_role": "SOLUTION_ARCHITECT"})
                    )
                    db.add(new_task)
                    await db.commit()
                    
                    # Echo back to terminal
                    await manager.broadcast(mission_id, {
                        "type": "system", 
                        "message": f"[User Input Acknowledged] Appended real-time task to the {mission.phase.value if hasattr(mission.phase, 'value') else mission.phase} phase queue."
                    })

    except WebSocketDisconnect:
        manager.disconnect(websocket, mission_id)

from backend.core.config import settings
import uuid

class CreditPolicy:
    """
    Central policy for determining credit costs and managing escrow holds.
    Requires server-side configuration. Does not hardcode prices.
    """

    @classmethod
    def _get_mission_cost(cls) -> int:
        if settings.MISSION_CREDIT_COST is None:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail="Billing policy not configured. MISSION_CREDIT_COST is not set.")
        return settings.MISSION_CREDIT_COST

    @classmethod
    async def get_balance(cls, db: AsyncSession, org_id: str) -> int:
        """
        Calculates the true balance from the ledger.
        """
        stmt = select(func.sum(LedgerTransaction.amount)).where(LedgerTransaction.organization_id == org_id)
        result = (await db.execute(stmt)).scalar()
        return result or 0

    @classmethod
    async def reserve_credits(cls, db: AsyncSession, org_id: str, mission_id: str) -> bool:
        """
        Attempts to reserve credits for a new mission.
        Raises HTTPException if insufficient balance.
        """
        cost = cls._get_mission_cost()
        
        # 1. Lock the organization to prevent race conditions during balance check
        stmt = select(Organization).where(Organization.id == org_id).with_for_update()
        org = (await db.execute(stmt)).scalars().first()
        
        if not org:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Organization not found")

        current_balance = await cls.get_balance(db, org_id)
            
        if current_balance < cost:
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=402, 
                detail=f"Insufficient credits. Required: {cost}, Available: {current_balance}"
            )
            
        # 2. Update denormalized balance for legacy support
        org.credit_balance = current_balance - cost
        
        # 3. Create Ledger entry
        tx = LedgerTransaction(
            id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
            organization_id=org_id,
            type=LedgerTransactionType.MISSION_RESERVATION,
            amount=-cost,
            reference_id=mission_id,
            metadata_json='{"status": "reserved"}'
        )
        db.add(tx)
        
        # Note: caller is responsible for db.commit() to ensure it's atomic with mission creation
        return True

    @classmethod
    async def release_reservation(cls, db: AsyncSession, org_id: str, mission_id: str):
        """Releases the held credits (refund) if mission fails or cancels."""
        # 1. Lock organization to prevent double-refund race condition
        stmt = select(Organization).where(Organization.id == org_id).with_for_update()
        org = (await db.execute(stmt)).scalars().first()
        if not org:
            return

        # Find original reservation
        stmt = select(LedgerTransaction).where(
            LedgerTransaction.reference_id == mission_id,
            LedgerTransaction.type == LedgerTransactionType.MISSION_RESERVATION
        )
        original = (await db.execute(stmt)).scalars().first()
        if not original:
            return # No reservation found
            
        # Check if already released or settled
        stmt = select(LedgerTransaction).where(
            LedgerTransaction.reference_id == mission_id,
            LedgerTransaction.type.in_([LedgerTransactionType.MISSION_RELEASE, LedgerTransactionType.MISSION_SETTLEMENT])
        )
        existing = (await db.execute(stmt)).scalars().first()
        if existing:
            return # Already handled
            
        cost = abs(original.amount)
        org.credit_balance += cost
            
        tx = LedgerTransaction(
            id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
            organization_id=org_id,
            type=LedgerTransactionType.MISSION_RELEASE,
            amount=cost,
            reference_id=mission_id,
            metadata_json='{"status": "released"}'
        )
        db.add(tx)
        await db.commit()

    @classmethod
    async def settle_reservation(cls, db: AsyncSession, org_id: str, mission_id: str):
        """Finalizes the held credits (consumes them) when mission succeeds."""
        # 1. Lock organization to prevent race condition
        stmt = select(Organization).where(Organization.id == org_id).with_for_update()
        org = (await db.execute(stmt)).scalars().first()
        if not org:
            return

        # Find original reservation
        stmt = select(LedgerTransaction).where(
            LedgerTransaction.reference_id == mission_id,
            LedgerTransaction.type == LedgerTransactionType.MISSION_RESERVATION
        )
        original = (await db.execute(stmt)).scalars().first()
        if not original:
            return # No reservation found

        # Check if already handled
        stmt = select(LedgerTransaction).where(
            LedgerTransaction.reference_id == mission_id,
            LedgerTransaction.type.in_([LedgerTransactionType.MISSION_RELEASE, LedgerTransactionType.MISSION_SETTLEMENT])
        )
        existing = (await db.execute(stmt)).scalars().first()
        if existing:
            return

        tx = LedgerTransaction(
            id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
            organization_id=org_id,
            type=LedgerTransactionType.MISSION_SETTLEMENT,
            amount=0, # The actual deduction was the reservation
            reference_id=mission_id,
            metadata_json='{"status": "Settled"}'
        )
        db.add(tx)
        await db.commit()

Token Bucket Rate Limiter
=========================
A thread-safe, lazy-refill token-bucket rate limiter implemented with
stdlib-only dependencies (time, threading, typing).

Algorithm (lazy refill):
    elapsed       = now - last_refill
    tokens_avail  = min(capacity, tokens_avail + elapsed * refill_rate_per_sec)

The bucket state is mutated only inside ``self._lock`` so the class is safe
for use across multiple threads.  An injectable ``now`` parameter on every
public mutating method enables fully deterministic unit tests without
monkeypatching the clock.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import threading
import time
from typing import Dict, Optional


class TokenBucketRateLimiter:
    """Thread-safe token-bucket rate limiter with injectable clock.

    Each unique *key* (e.g. a user-id, IP address, or API client identifier)
    maintains its own independent bucket.  Buckets are created lazily on first
    access; an unseen key is always treated as a full bucket.

    Parameters
    ----------
    capacity:
        Maximum number of tokens a bucket may hold.  Must be > 0.
    refill_rate_per_sec:
        Number of tokens added to a bucket per second of elapsed wall time.
        Must be > 0.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``capacity <= 0`` or ``refill_rate_per_sec <= 0``.
    """

    def __init__(self, capacity: float, refill_rate_per_sec: float) -> None:
        """Initialise the rate limiter.

        Parameters
        ----------
        capacity:
            Maximum token capacity per bucket.
        refill_rate_per_sec:
            Token refill speed (tokens per second).

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``capacity <= 0`` or ``refill_rate_per_sec <= 0``.
        """
        if capacity <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"capacity must be > 0, got {capacity!r}"
            )
        if refill_rate_per_sec <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"refill_rate_per_sec must be > 0, got {refill_rate_per_sec!r}"
            )

        self._capacity: float = capacity
        self._refill_rate: float = refill_rate_per_sec
        self._buckets: Dict[str, Dict[str, float]] = {}
        self._lock: threading.Lock = threading.Lock()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Internal helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _get_or_create_bucket(self, key: str, now: float) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """Return the bucket for *key*, creating a full one if absent.

        **Must be called while holding** ``self._lock``.

        Parameters
        ----------
        key:
            Bucket identifier.
        now:
            Current monotonic timestamp (used as ``last_refill`` for new
            buckets so that no phantom elapsed time is credited).

        Returns
        -------
        Dict[str, float]
            The live (mutable) bucket dict ``{'tokens': float, 'last_refill': float}``.
        """
        if key not in self._buckets:
            self._buckets[key] = {
                "tokens": self._capacity,
                "last_refill": now,
            }
        return self._buckets[key]

    def _refill_bucket(self, bucket: Dict[str, float], now: float) -> None:
        """Apply lazy token refill to *bucket* in-place.

        **Must be called while holding** ``self._lock``.

        Parameters
        ----------
        bucket:
            Mutable bucket dict obtained from ``_get_or_create_bucket``.
        now:
            Current monotonic timestamp.
        """
        elapsed: float = now - bucket["last_refill"]
        if elapsed > 0:
            bucket["tokens"] = min(
                self._capacity,
                bucket["tokens"] + elapsed * self._refill_rate,
            )
            bucket["last_refill"] = now

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Public API
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def allow_request(
        self,
        key: str,
        tokens: float = 1,
        now: Optional[float] = None,
    ) -> bool:
        """Attempt to consume *tokens* from the bucket identified by *key*.

        Parameters
        ----------
        key:
            Identifies the rate-limited entity (e.g. user-id, IP).
        tokens:
            Number of tokens to consume.  Must be > 0.
        now:
            Override the monotonic clock for deterministic testing.  When

        Returns
        -------
        bool

            ``False`` if the bucket had insufficient tokens (no mutation).

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``tokens <= 0``.

        Notes
        -----
        * If ``tokens > capacity`` this method always returns ``False``
          without touching any bucket state, because the request can never
          be satisfied regardless of how full the bucket is.
        * All reads and writes to ``self._buckets`` are performed while
          holding ``self._lock`` so the method is thread-safe.

        if tokens <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"tokens must be > 0, got {tokens!r}"
            )

        # A request that exceeds the bucket's maximum can never be satisfied.
        if tokens > self._capacity:
            return False

        resolved_now: float = time.monotonic() if now is None else now

        with self._lock:
            bucket = self._get_or_create_bucket(key, resolved_now)
            self._refill_bucket(bucket, resolved_now)

            if bucket["tokens"] >= tokens:
                bucket["tokens"] -= tokens
                bucket["last_refill"] = resolved_now
                return True

            return False

    def get_Bucket_state(self, key: str, now: Optional[float] = None) -> dict:
        """Return a snapshot of the current bucket state for *key*.

        The bucket is lazily refilled before the snapshot is taken, so the
        returned ``tokens`` value reflects the current available capacity.

        Parameters

        key:

        now:
            Override the monotonic clock (useful for deterministic tests).
            When ``None`` (the default) ``time.monotonic()`` is used.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            A **copy** of ``{'tokens': float, 'last_refill': float}``.
            Mutating the returned dict has no effect on internal state.
            For an unknown key a full-capacity state dict is returned
            (no ``KeyError`` is raised); the key is **not** inserted into
            ``self._buckets`` by this call.

        Notes
        -----
        All reads and writes to ``self._buckets`` are performed while
        holding ``self._lock`` so the method is thread-safe.
        """
        resolved_now: float = time.monotonic() if now is None else now

        with self._lock:
            if key not in self._buckets:
                # Return a synthetic full-capacity snapshot without
                # persisting any new bucket entry.
                return {"tokens": self._capacity, "last_refill": resolved_now}

            bucket = self._buckets[key]
            self._refill_bucket(bucket, resolved_now)
            # Return an independent copy so the caller cannot mutate internals.
            return {"tokens": bucket["tokens"], "last_refill": bucket["last_refill"]}

class TestConcurrencySafety:
    """Concurrent allow_request calls must never over-subscribe the bucket."""

    def test_concurrent_threads_never_oversubscribe(self) -> None:
        """Total tokens admitted by N threads must never exceed the bucket capacity."""
        capacity = 100.0
        limiter = TokenBucketRateLimiter(capacity=capacity, refill_rate_per_sec=0.0001)

        key = "shared_key"
        # Warm up the bucket so all threads see the same starting state.
        now_base = 1000.0
        # Force bucket creation at a controlled time.
        with limiter._lock:
            limiter._buckets[key] = {"tokens": capacity, "last_refill": now_base}

        admitted: List[bool] = []
        errors: List[Exception] = []

        def worker(thread_id: int) -> None:
            try:
                # Each thread uses the same `now` so no refill occurs;
                # only the initial capacity is up for grabs.
                result = limiter.allow_request(key, tokens=1.0, now=now_base)
                admitted.append(result)
            except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover
                errors.append(exc)

        n_threads = 200
        threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(i,)) for i in range(n_threads)]
        for t in threads:
            t.start()
        for t in threads:
            t.join()

        assert errors == [], f"Unexpected exceptions: {errors}"

        total_admitted = sum(1 for r in admitted if r is True)
        # Must never admit more tokens than the bucket held.
        assert total_admitted <= int(capacity), (
            f"Over-subscribed: admitted {total_admitted} but capacity was {capacity}"
        )

    def test_concurrent_independent_keys_no_interference(self) -> None:
        """Concurrent access on different keys must not cause cross-key corruption."""
        capacity = 10.0
        limiter = TokenBucketRateLimiter(capacity=capacity, refill_rate_per_sec=0.001)
        results: dict[str, int] = {}
        lock = threading.Lock()

        def drain_key(key: str) -> None:
            admitted = 0
            t0 = 5000.0
            for _ in range(int(capacity) + 5):  # try to exceed capacity
                if limiter.allow_request(key, tokens=1.0, now=t0):
                    admitted += 1
            with lock:
                results[key] = admitted

        keys = [f"key_{i}" for i in range(10)]
        threads = [threading.Thread(target=drain_key, args=(k,)) for k in keys]
        for t in threads:
            t.start()
        for t in threads:
            t.join()

        for key, admitted in results.items():
            assert admitted <= int(capacity), (
                f"Key {key!r} over-subscribed: admitted {admitted}"
            )

Token Bucket Rate Limiter
=========================
A thread-safe, lazy-refill token-bucket rate limiter implemented with
stdlib-only dependencies (time, threading, typing).

Algorithm (lazy refill):
    elapsed       = now - last_refill
    tokens_avail  = min(capacity, tokens_avail + elapsed * refill_rate_per_sec)

The bucket state is mutated only inside ``self._lock`` so the class is safe
for use across multiple threads.  An injectable ``now`` parameter on every
public mutating method enables fully deterministic unit tests without
monkeypatching the clock.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import threading
import time
from typing import Dict, Optional


class TokenBucketRateLimiter:
    """Thread-safe token-bucket rate limiter with injectable clock.

    Each unique *key* (e.g. a user-id, IP address, or API client identifier)
    maintains its own independent bucket.  Buckets are created lazily on first
    access; an unseen key is always treated as a full bucket.

    Parameters
    ----------
    capacity:
        Maximum number of tokens a bucket may hold.  Must be > 0.
    refill_rate_per_sec:
        Number of tokens added to a bucket per second of elapsed wall time.
        Must be > 0.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``capacity <= 0`` or ``refill_rate_per_sec <= 0``.
    """

    def __init__(self, capacity: float, refill_rate_per_sec: float) -> None:
        """Initialise the rate limiter.

        Parameters
        ----------
        capacity:
            Maximum token capacity per bucket.
        refill_rate_per_sec:
            Token refill speed (tokens per second).

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``capacity <= 0`` or ``refill_rate_per_sec <= 0``.
        """
        if capacity <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"capacity must be > 0, got {capacity!r}"
            )
        if refill_rate_per_sec <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"refill_rate_per_sec must be > 0, got {refill_rate_per_sec!r}"
            )

        self._capacity: float = capacity
        self._refill_rate: float = refill_rate_per_sec
        self._buckets: Dict[str, Dict[str, float]] = {}
        self._lock: threading.Lock = threading.Lock()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Internal helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _get_or_create_bucket(self, key: str, now: float) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """Return the bucket for *key*, creating a full one if absent.

        **Must be called while holding** ``self._lock``.

        Parameters
        ----------
        key:
            Bucket identifier.
        now:
            Current monotonic timestamp (used as ``last_refill`` for new
            buckets so that no phantom elapsed time is credited).

        Returns
        -------
        Dict[str, float]
            The live (mutable) bucket dict ``{'tokens': float, 'last_refill': float}``.
        """
        if key not in self._buckets:
            self._buckets[key] = {
                "tokens": self._capacity,
                "last_refill": now,
            }
        return self._buckets[key]

    def _refill_bucket(self, bucket: Dict[str, float], now: float) -> None:
        """Apply lazy token refill to *bucket* in-place.

        **Must be called while holding** ``self._lock``.

        Parameters
        ----------
        bucket:
            Mutable bucket dict obtained from ``_get_or_create_bucket``.
        now:
            Current monotonic timestamp.
        """
        elapsed: float = now - bucket["last_refill"]
        if elapsed > 0:
            bucket["tokens"] = min(
                self._capacity,
                bucket["tokens"] + elapsed * self._refill_rate,
            )
            bucket["last_refill"] = now

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Public API
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def allow_request(
        self,
        key: str,
        tokens: float = 1,
        now: Optional[float] = None,
    ) -> bool:
        """Attempt to consume *tokens* from the bucket identified by *key*.

        Parameters
        ----------
        key:
            Identifies the rate-limited entity (e.g. user-id, IP).
        tokens:
            Number of tokens to consume.  Must be > 0.
        now:
            Override the monotonic clock for deterministic testing.  When
            ``None`` (the default) ``time.monotonic()`` is used.

        Returns
        -------
        bool
            ``True`` if the request is admitted (tokens were deducted);
            ``False`` if the bucket had insufficient tokens (no mutation).

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``tokens <= 0``.

        Notes
        -----
        * If ``tokens > capacity`` this method always returns ``False``
          without touching any bucket state, because the request can never
          be satisfied regardless of how full the bucket is.
        * All reads and writes to ``self._buckets`` are performed while
          holding ``self._lock`` so the method is thread-safe.
        """
        if tokens <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"tokens must be > 0, got {tokens!r}"
            )

        # A request that exceeds the bucket's maximum can never be satisfied.
        if tokens > self._capacity:
            return False

        resolved_now: float = time.monotonic() if now is None else now

        with self._lock:
            bucket = self._get_or_create_bucket(key, resolved_now)
            self._refill_bucket(bucket, resolved_now)

            if bucket["tokens"] >= tokens:
                bucket["tokens"] -= tokens
                bucket["last_refill"] = resolved_now
                return True

            return False

    def get_Bucket_state(self, key: str, now: Optional[float] = None) -> dict:
        """Return a snapshot of the current bucket state for *key*.

        The bucket is lazily refilled before the snapshot is taken, so the
        returned ``tokens`` value reflects the current available capacity.

        Parameters
        ----------
        key:
            Bucket identifier to inspect.
        now:
            Override the monotonic clock (useful for deterministic tests).
            When ``None`` (the default) ``time.monotonic()`` is used.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            A **copy** of ``{'tokens': float, 'last_refill': float}``.
            Mutating the returned dict has no effect on internal state.
            For an unknown key a full-capacity state dict is returned
            (no ``KeyError`` is raised); the key is **not** inserted into
            ``self._buckets`` by this call.

        Notes
        -----
        All reads and writes to ``self._buckets`` are performed while
        holding ``self._lock`` so the method is thread-safe.
        """
        resolved_now: float = time.monotonic() if now is None else now

        with self._lock:
            if key not in self._buckets:
                # Return a synthetic full-capacity snapshot without
                # persisting any new bucket entry.
                return {"tokens": self._capacity, "last_refill": resolved_now}

            bucket = self._buckets[key]
            self._refill_bucket(bucket, resolved_now)
            # Return an independent copy so the caller cannot mutate internals.
            return {"tokens": bucket["tokens"], "last_refill": bucket["last_refill"]}

    def test_concurrent_independent_keys_no_interference(self) -> None:
        """Concurrent access on different keys must not cause cross-key corruption."""
        capacity = 10.0
        limiter = TokenBucketRateLimiter(capacity=capacity, refill_rate_per_sec=0.001)
        results: dict[str, int] = {}
        lock = threading.Lock()

        def drain_key(key: str) -> None:
            admitted = 0
            t0 = 5000.0
            for _ in range(int(capacity) + 5):  # try to exceed capacity

            with lock:

        for t in threads:
            t.join()

        for key, admitted in results.items():
            assert admitted <= int(capacity), (

A mobile-first, installable marketplace experience for hiring affordable AI specialists through fixed-price packages. It includes a general workspace layer where users can connect work tools, give agents context, review risky decisions, and see activity reports. The prototype includes agent discovery, search and filters, detailed listings, three package tiers, simulated escrow, delivery acceptance/revisions, buyer orders, wallet, activity reporting, and a four-step creator listing flow.

## Open it

Open `index.html` in any modern browser. For the installable/offline experience, serve this folder from any static web host (for example, GitHub Pages, Netlify, or Vercel) and open it on a phone.

## What is connected in this prototype

- Search, category selection, price/rating filters, listing details, work tabs, task briefs, messaging, and agent creation are interactive.
- New tasks, messages, and creator listings are saved locally in the browser so the prototype remains usable after a refresh.
- The app uses realistic local marketplace data. Replace the local data functions in `app.js` with API calls when connecting the production backend.

## Production handoff

The supplied brief’s server requirements—Next.js API routes, Prisma/Postgres, authentication, Stripe Connect 80/20 transfers, moderation, messaging persistence, and S3 uploads—should be implemented behind these screens before public launch. A mobile-first, installable marketplace experience for hiring affordable AI specialists through fixed-price packages. The current front end can now call `POST /api/run-agent`, which is a Netlify Function. The API key stays on Netlify and is never placed in the browser or in this repository.

## Private test only

2. In Netlify, open **Project configuration → Environment variables**.

6. Deploy again. Place an order and the delivery will come from the server function, not the local demo preview.

## Before public launch

Do **not** leave `KOBITS_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_DEMO=true` on a public site. Add real user authentication, per-user rate limits, payments, and a database first. Then change the function so it verifies the signed-in user before calling the AI provider.

## Gmail and Slack

Gmail and Slack require separate OAuth applications, redirect URLs, encrypted token storage, and user consent. They are not enabled by simply adding an API key. Build them after the order execution path and authentication are working.

**Kobits — AI agents that get real work done.**

Kobits is a buyer-first marketplace for task-focused AI agents. People can browse agents for research, customer support, content, data clean-up, sales outreach, video planning, and more; choose a clear fixed-price package; and receive a structured delivery.

## What is included

- Responsive marketplace and installable web app in `outputs/agently-mobile/`
- Secure serverless agent runner in `netlify/functions/`
- Browser extension starter in `extensions/kobits-browser/`
- Embeddable website widget in `widget/`
- Agent task guardrails, scoped deliveries, order tracking, agent pages, and demo escrow flows

## Run locally

Open `outputs/agently-mobile/index.html` for the visual demo.

For real agent execution, deploy through Netlify, add `OPENAI_API_KEY` as a server-side environment variable, and follow [REAL_AGENT_SETUP.md](REAL_AGENT_SETUP.md). Never put API keys in browser code.

## Deploy

`netlify.toml` publishes the app from `outputs/agently-mobile` and deploys the serverless functions from `netlify/functions`.

## Built with Codex and GPT-5.6

Kobits was created with Codex and GPT-5.6 as an AI development partner. We used it to turn the marketplace idea into a working responsive product, build the buyer-first flows and agent pages, create the secure Netlify agent-function structure, improve interaction details, and test the project structure. The team directed the product vision, reviewed the output, and made the final decisions.

## Status

This repository contains a working prototype and deployment-ready structure. Payments, accounts, and production data storage require their own secure services before a public launch.

The pricing model targets a minimum 5% net profit after variable delivery costs. The calculation is:

utils/validator.py
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Email validation utility for the Kobits platform.

Provides:
  - ``is_valid_email(email)``       -> bool
  - ``validate_email(email)``       -> raises ``ValueError`` on invalid input
  - ``normalize_email(email)``      -> lowercase-normalised address string
  - ``ValidationResult`` dataclass  -> structured result with details

Design decisions
----------------
* Zero external dependencies – relies solely on Python stdlib (``re``).
* Follows RFC 5321 / RFC 5322 practical rules used by real MTAs:
    - Local part:  printable ASCII excluding space; max 64 chars.
    - Domain part: labels of 1-63 chars (alphanum + hyphen, not at
                   start/end); at least one dot; max 255 chars total.
    - Total length: <= 254 chars (RFC 5321 §4.5.3).
* Deliberately rejects technically-valid-but-impractical addresses such
  as quoted local parts or IP-address domains, matching the behaviour
  expected by most web applications.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Optional

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Internal compiled patterns
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Local part: alphanumeric + . _ % + - (no consecutive dots, no leading/trailing dot)
_LOCAL_RE = re.compile(
    r"^[a-zA-Z0-9]"                  # must start with alphanum
    r"(?:[a-zA-Z0-9._%+\-]*"         # middle chars (greedy)
    r"[a-zA-Z0-9])?$"                # must end with alphanum (|single char already covered)
)

# Single local part character (i.e. a one-character address like "a@b.com")
_LOCAL_SINGLE_CHAR_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-zA-Z0-9]$")

# Domain label: starts and ends with alphanum, may contain hyphens in the middle
_DOMAIN_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-zA-Z0-9]([a-zA-Z0-9\-]*[a-zA-Z0-9])?$")

# TLD: at least 2 alpha chars (no digits, no hyphens)
_TLD_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-zA-Z]{2,}$")

# Max lengths (RFC 5321)
_MAX_LOCAL_LEN: int = 64
_MAX_DOMAIN_LEN: int = 255
_MAX_EMAIL_LEN: int = 254


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Public data structure
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class ValidationResult:
    """Structured result returned by :func:`validate_email_result`."""

    email: str
    """The original (un-normalised) input string."""

    is_valid: bool
    """``True`` when the address passes all checks."""

    local_part: Optional[str] = field(default=None)
    """Local part (before ``@``), populated on valid addresses."""

    domain: Optional[str] = field(default=None)
    """Domain part (after ``@``), populated on valid addresses."""

    normalized: Optional[str] = field(default=None)
    """Lowercased version of the full address, populated on valid addresses."""

    error: Optional[str] = field(default=None)
    """Human-readable reason for rejection, populated on invalid addresses."""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Core helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _validate_local(local: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """Return ``None`` on success or an error message string on failure."""
    if not local:
        return "Local part must not be empty."
    if len(local) > _MAX_LOCAL_LEN:
        return f"Local part exceeds {_MAX_LOCAL_LEN} characters."
    if ".." in local:
        return "Local part must not contain consecutive dots."
    # Single-character local part is valid (e.g. "a@example.com")
    if len(local) == 1:
        if not _LOCAL_SINGLE_CHAR_RE.match(local):
            return "Local part contains an invalid character."
        return None
    if not _LOCAL_RE.match(local):
        return "Local part contains an invalid character or structure."
    return None


def _validate_domain(domain: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """Return ``None`` on success or an error message string on failure."""
    if not domain:
        return "Domain part must not be empty."
    if len(domain) > _MAX_DOMAIN_LEN:
        return f"Domain exceeds {_MAX_DOMAIN_LEN} characters."
    if domain.startswith(".") or domain.endswith("."):
        return "Domain must not start or end with a dot."
    if ".." in domain:
        return "Domain must not contain consecutive dots."

    labels = domain.split(".")
    if len(labels) < 2:
        return "Domain must contain at least one dot."

    for label in labels:
        if not label:
            return "Domain contains an empty label."
        if len(label) > 63:
            return f"Domain label '{label}' exceeds 63 characters."
        if not _DOMAIN_LABEL_RE.match(label):
            return f"Domain label '{label}' contains an invalid character or structure."

    # TLD must be all-alpha, at least 2 chars
    tld = labels[-1]
    if not _TLD_RE.match(tld):
        return f"Top-level domain '{tld}' is invalid (must be 2+ alpha characters)."

    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Public API
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def is_valid_email(email: str) -> bool:
    """Return ``True`` if *email* is a valid email address, ``False`` otherwise.

    Parameters
    ----------
    email:
        The string to validate.  ``None`` and non-string values are safely
        handled and return ``False``.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> is_valid_email("user@example.com")
    True
    >>> is_valid_email("not-an-email")
    False
    """
    if not isinstance(email, str):
        return False

    email = email.strip()

    if not email or len(email) > _MAX_EMAIL_LEN:
        return False

    at_count = email.count("@")
    if at_count != 1:
        return False

    local, domain = email.split("@", 1)
    return _validate_local(local) is None and _validate_domain(domain) is None


def validate_email(email: str) -> str:
    """Validate *email* and return the normalised (lowercased) address.

    Parameters
    ----------
    email:
        The email string to validate.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        The lowercased, stripped version of *email*.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        With a descriptive message if *email* fails any validation rule.
    TypeError
        If *email* is not a string.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> validate_email("User@Example.COM")
    'user@example.com'
    >>> validate_email("bad@")
    Traceback (most recent call last):
        ...
    ValueError: Domain part must not be empty.
    """
    if not isinstance(email, str):
        raise TypeError(f"Expected a string, got {type(email).__name__!r}.")

    email_stripped = email.strip()

    if not email_stripped:
        raise ValueError("Email address must not be empty.")
    if len(email_stripped) > _MAX_EMAIL_LEN:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Email address exceeds maximum length of {_MAX_EMAIL_LEN} characters."
        )

    at_count = email_stripped.count("@")
    if at_count == 0:
        raise ValueError("Email address must contain an '@' symbol.")
    if at_count > 1:
        raise ValueError("Email address must contain exactly one '@' symbol.")

    local, domain = email_stripped.split("@", 1)

    local_err = _validate_local(local)
    if local_err:
        raise ValueError(local_err)

    domain_err = _validate_domain(domain)
    if domain_err:
        raise ValueError(domain_err)

    return email_stripped.lower()


def normalize_email(email: str) -> str:
    """Return the lowercased, stripped email address.

    Convenience wrapper around :func:`validate_email` for callers that want
    to normalise valid addresses without catching exceptions themselves.

    Parameters
    ----------
    email:
        A *valid* email string.  Raises :exc:`ValueError` on invalid input
        (same as :func:`validate_email`).

    Examples
    --------
    >>> normalize_email("  Alice@Example.ORG  ")
    'alice@example.org'
    """
    return validate_email(email)


def validate_email_result(email: str) -> ValidationResult:
    """Validate *email* and return a :class:`ValidationResult` instance.

    Unlike :func:`validate_email`, this function never raises; it always
    returns a structured result object.

    Parameters
    ----------
    email:
        The string to validate (any type is accepted; non-strings are
        reported as invalid).

    Examples
    --------
    >>> r = validate_email_result("user@example.com")
    >>> r.is_valid
    True
    >>> r.normalized
    'user@example.com'

    >>> r = validate_email_result("bad@@example.com")
    >>> r.is_valid
    False
    >>> r.error
    'Email address must contain exactly one \\'@\\' symbol.'
    """
    try:
        normalised = validate_email(email)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        local, domain = normalised.split("@", 1)
        return ValidationResult(
            email=email,
            is_valid=True,
            local_part=local,
            domain=domain,
            normalized=normalised,
        )
    except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
        return ValidationResult(
            email=str(email) if not isinstance(email, str) else email,
            is_valid=False,
            error=str(exc),
        )


__all__ = [
    "ValidationResult",
    "is_valid_email",
    "validate_email",
    "normalize_email",
    "validate_email_result",
]

    """Tests for :func:`normalize_email`."""

    def test_lowercases_address(self) -> None:
        assert normalize_email("ADMIN@EXAMPLE.COM") == "admin@example.com"

    def test_strips_whitespace(self) -> None:
        assert normalize_email("  hello@world.org  ") == "hello@world.org"

    def test_preserves_already_lowercase(self) -> None:
        email = "user@example.com"
        assert normalize_email(email) == email

    def test_raises_on_invalid_email(self) -> None:
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            normalize_email("not-an-email")

    def test_raises_on_none(self) -> None:
        with pytest.raises(TypeError):
            normalize_email(None)  # type: ignore[arg-type]

class TestValidateEmailResult:
    """Tests for :func:`validate_email_result`."""

    def test_returns_validation_result_type(self) -> None:
        result = validate_email_result("user@example.com")
        assert isinstance(result, ValidationResult)

    def test_valid_email_populates_all_fields(self) -> None:
        result = validate_email_result("User@Example.COM")
        assert result.is_valid is True
        assert result.local_part == "user"
        assert result.domain == "example.com"
        assert result.normalized == "user@example.com"
        assert result.email == "User@Example.COM"
        assert result.error is None

    def test_invalid_email_populates_error_field(self) -> None:
        result = validate_email_result("not-an-email")
        assert result.is_valid is False
        assert result.error is not None
        assert len(result.error) > 0
        assert result.local_part is None
        assert result.domain is None
        assert result.normalized is None

    def test_empty_string_is_invalid(self) -> None:
        result = validate_email_result("")
        assert result.is_valid is False
        assert result.error is not None

    def test_none_input_is_invalid(self) -> None:
        result = validate_email_result(None)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        assert result.is_valid is False
        assert result.error is not None

    def test_integer_input_is_invalid(self) -> None:
        result = validate_email_result(42)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        assert result.is_valid is False
        assert result.error is not None

    def test_multiple_at_signs_is_invalid(self) -> None:
        result = validate_email_result("a@@b.com")
        assert result.is_valid is False
        assert "exactly one" in result.error.lower() or "@" in result.error

    def test_email_stored_verbatim(self) -> None:
        """Original (un-normalised) email is stored in `.email`."""
        raw = "Admin@Example.COM"
        result = validate_email_result(raw)
        assert result.email == raw

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("email", VALID_EMAILS)
    def test_all_valid_emails_produce_valid_result(self, email: str) -> None:

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("email", INVALID_EMAILS)

    def test_subdomains_are_preserved_in_domain_field(self) -> None:

        result = validate_email_result("user+tag@example.com")
        assert result.local_part == "user+tag"

class TestEdgeCases:
    """Boundary and edge-case tests."""

    def test_exactly_254_chars_is_valid(self) -> None:
        # 64 local + 1 @ + 185 domain (3x labels + .com) = 254
        local = "a" * 64
        # Build a domain that totals 254 - 64 - 1 = 189 chars
        # e.g. "bbb...bbb.ccc...ccc.com" (three-label domain)
        label1 = "b" * 63
        label2 = "c" * 63
        # Remaining = 189 - 63 - 1 - 63 - 1 = 61; split as label + .tld
        remaining = 189 - 63 - 1 - 63 - 1  # = 61
        tld_len = 3   # "com"
        label3 = "d" * (remaining - tld_len - 1)
        domain = f"{label1}.{label2}.{label3}.com"
        email = f"{local}@{domain}"
        assert len(email) <= 254
        assert is_valid_email(email) is True

    def test_255_chars_is_invalid(self) -> None:
        """An address exceeding 254 chars must be rejected."""
        email = "a" * 64 + "@" + "b" * 60 + "." + "c" * 60 + "." + "d" * 60 + ".com"
        if len(email) > 254:
            assert is_valid_email(email) is False

LRU Cache implementation with capacity-based eviction.

Uses an OrderedDict for O(1) get/put operations.
The least-recently-used item is evicted when the cache reaches capacity.
"""

from collections import OrderedDict
from typing import Any, Optional


class LRUCache:
    """
    A Least Recently Used (LRU) Cache with a fixed capacity.

    When the cache is full and a new item is inserted, the least recently
    used item (the one not accessed for the longest time) is evicted.

    Operations:
        get(key)        -> value or -1 if not found  (O(1))
        put(key, value) -> None, evicts LRU if needed (O(1))

    Example:
        >>> cache = LRUCache(capacity=2)
        >>> cache.put(1, "a")
        >>> cache.put(2, "b")
        >>> cache.get(1)
        'a'
        >>> cache.put(3, "c")   # evicts key 2 (LRU)
        >>> cache.get(2)        # -1, evicted
        -1
    """

    def __init__(self, capacity: int) -> None:
        if capacity <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"Capacity must be a positive integer, got {capacity!r}")
        self.capacity: int = capacity
        # OrderedDict preserves insertion order; we use move_to_end to track recency.
        # The *oldest* (least recently used) item sits at the front (last=False end).
        self._cache: OrderedDict = OrderedDict()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Public API
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def get(self, key: Any) -> Any:
        """
        Return the value associated with *key* if it exists, else -1.
        Accessing a key promotes it to 'most recently used'.
        """
        if key not in self._cache:
            return -1
        # Move to end → marks as most recently used
        self._cache.move_to_end(key)
        return self._cache[key]

    def put(self, key: Any, value: Any) -> None:
        """
        Insert or update *key* with *value*.
        If the cache is at capacity and *key* is new, the LRU item is evicted first.
        Updating an existing key also promotes it to most recently used.
        """
        if key in self._cache:
            # Update value and promote to most-recently-used
            self._cache.move_to_end(key)
            self._cache[key] = value
        else:
            if len(self._cache) >= self.capacity:
                # Evict the least recently used item (first item in OrderedDict)
                self._cache.popitem(last=False)
            self._cache[key] = value

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Convenience helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        """Return the current number of items in the cache."""
        return len(self._cache)

    def __contains__(self, key: Any) -> bool:
        """Support the ``in`` operator without affecting LRU order."""
        return key in self._cache

    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover
        items = list(self._cache.items())
        return f"LRUCache(capacity={self.capacity}, items={items})"

    def keys(self) -> list:
        """Return cache keys from LRU (oldest) to MRU (newest)."""
        return list(self._cache.keys())

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Remove all items from the cache."""
        self._cache.clear()

5 pytest test cases for the LRUCache class in cache.py.

Each test is independent and covers a distinct behavioural aspect:
  1. Basic put/get operations (hit and miss)
  2. LRU eviction when capacity is exceeded
  3. Accessing a key refreshes its recency (prevents eviction)
  4. Updating an existing key updates value and refreshes recency
  5. Edge-cases: capacity-1 cache and invalid capacity raise ValueError
"""

import pytest
from cache import LRUCache


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Test 1 – Basic put / get (cache hit and miss)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_basic_put_and_get():
    """
    put() stores key-value pairs; get() retrieves them.
    get() on a missing key returns -1.
    """
    cache = LRUCache(capacity=3)

    cache.put("name", "Alice")
    cache.put("age", 30)
    cache.put("city", "Paris")

    assert cache.get("name") == "Alice"
    assert cache.get("age") == 30
    assert cache.get("city") == "Paris"

    # Key that was never inserted
    assert cache.get("country") == -1
    assert cache.get(999) == -1


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Test 2 – LRU eviction when capacity is exceeded
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_lru_eviction_on_capacity_overflow():
    """
    When a new key is inserted into a full cache the *least recently used*
    entry (the one untouched the longest) must be evicted.
    """
    cache = LRUCache(capacity=2)

    cache.put(1, "one")
    cache.put(2, "two")

    # Cache is full: [1→"one", 2→"two"].  Key 1 is LRU.
    cache.put(3, "three")   # must evict key 1 (LRU)

    assert cache.get(1) == -1,  "Key 1 should have been evicted (LRU)"
    assert cache.get(2) == "two"
    assert cache.get(3) == "three"
    assert len(cache) == 2


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Test 3 – Accessing a key refreshes its recency (prevents premature eviction)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_get_refreshes_recency():
    """
    Calling get() on an existing key must promote it to 'most recently used',
    so a *different* (less recently used) key gets evicted on the next insert.
    """
    cache = LRUCache(capacity=2)

    cache.put("x", 10)
    cache.put("y", 20)

    # Access "x" → "x" is now MRU; "y" becomes LRU
    assert cache.get("x") == 10

    # Insert new key → "y" should be evicted (LRU), NOT "x"
    cache.put("z", 30)

    assert cache.get("x") == 10,  "'x' was recently used and must survive"
    assert cache.get("y") == -1,  "'y' was LRU and must be evicted"
    assert cache.get("z") == 30


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Test 4 – Updating an existing key updates value and refreshes recency
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_update_existing_key_refreshes_recency():
    """
    put() on an *existing* key must:
      a) update its stored value, and
      b) mark it as most recently used (so it isn't the next eviction victim).
    """
    cache = LRUCache(capacity=2)

    cache.put("a", 1)
    cache.put("b", 2)

    # Update "a" → "a" becomes MRU; "b" is now LRU
    cache.put("a", 100)

    # Insert new key → "b" should be evicted (LRU), NOT "a"
    cache.put("c", 3)

    assert cache.get("a") == 100, "Updated value should be 100"
    assert cache.get("b") == -1,  "'b' was LRU and must be evicted"
    assert cache.get("c") == 3
    assert len(cache) == 2


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Test 5 – Edge cases: capacity-1 cache and invalid capacity
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_edge_cases_capacity_one_and_invalid_capacity():
    """
    a) A cache of capacity=1 should always hold only one item;
       every new put() evicts the previous entry.
    b) Constructing an LRUCache with capacity <= 0 must raise ValueError.
    """
    # --- 5a: capacity-1 behaviour ---
    cache = LRUCache(capacity=1)

    cache.put("only", "first")
    assert cache.get("only") == "first"

    cache.put("only2", "second")   # evicts "only"
    assert cache.get("only") == -1,   "'only' must be evicted"
    assert cache.get("only2") == "second"
    assert len(cache) == 1

    # Re-insert the same key → no eviction needed (capacity still 1)
    cache.put("only2", "updated")
    assert cache.get("only2") == "updated"
    assert len(cache) == 1

    # --- 5b: invalid capacity raises ValueError ---
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        LRUCache(capacity=0)

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        LRUCache(capacity=-5)

@contextlib.asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    # Validate provider configuration on startup
    from backend.core.config import settings
    from backend.services.llm import get_llm_provider
    try:
        get_llm_provider()
    except Exception as e:
        if settings.REAL_AI_TEST:
            # Hard crash if REAL_AI_TEST is enabled and provider is misconfigured
            raise e
        print(f"Warning: Provider misconfigured: {e}")

    # Database tables should be created via migrations in production.
    # In development/tests, we still use create_all if needed, but 
    # it's better to rely on alembic.
    if settings.KOBITS_DEV_MODE:
        async with engine.begin() as conn:
            await conn.run_sync(Base.metadata.create_all)

    # Resume ACTIVE missions and clear dangling locks
    from backend.core.database import AsyncSessionLocal
    from backend.models.mission import Mission, MissionStatus
    from backend.services.mission_runtime import MissionRuntime
    import asyncio
    from sqlalchemy import select, update
    
    async with AsyncSessionLocal() as db:
        from datetime import datetime, timezone
        # Clear any dangling locks that have expired
        stmt = (
            update(Mission)
            .where(Mission.execution_lock_id != None)
            .where(
                (Mission.execution_lock_expires_at == None) | 
                (Mission.execution_lock_expires_at < datetime.now(timezone.utc))
            )
            .values(execution_lock_id=None, execution_lock_expires_at=None)
        )
        await db.execute(stmt)
        await db.commit()
        
        # Resume active missions that aren't currently locked
        stmt = (
            select(Mission)
            .where(Mission.status == MissionStatus.ACTIVE)
            .where(Mission.execution_lock_id == None)
        )
        res = await db.execute(stmt)
        for m in res.scalars().all():
            print(f"Resuming active mission {m.id}")
            asyncio.create_task(MissionRuntime(m.id, m.organization_id, m.created_by).execute())

    # Load custom tools from database into ToolRegistry
    from backend.api.v1.tools import load_custom_tools_on_startup
    await load_custom_tools_on_startup()

    yield
    await engine.dispose()

from fastapi import WebSocket, WebSocketDisconnect
import json

from backend.services.websocket_manager import manager
import uuid
from backend.core.database import AsyncSessionLocal
from backend.models.project import Task, TaskStatus
from backend.models.mission import Mission

@app.websocket("/ws/terminal/{mission_id}")
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket, mission_id: str):
    await manager.connect(websocket, mission_id)
    try:
        # Acknowledge connection
        await websocket.send_json({"type": "system", "message": f"Connected to Mission {mission_id} live terminal."})
        while True:
            data = await websocket.receive_text()
            
            # Parse user input
            try:
                payload = json.loads(data)
                text = payload.get("message", payload.get("content", data))
            except Exception:
                text = data
                
            if not text or not str(text).strip():
                continue
                
            # Connect the terminal input to the active API/LLM pipeline
            async with AsyncSessionLocal() as db:
                mission = await db.get(Mission, mission_id)
                if mission:
                    new_task = Task(
                        id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
                        mission_id=mission.id,
                        project_id=mission.project_id,
                        created_by=mission.created_by,
                        title="Process User Feedback",
                        description=f"The user has provided live input/feedback:\n\n\"{text}\"\n\nPlease analyze this and adjust the mission trajectory accordingly.",
                        status=TaskStatus.PENDING,
                        phase=mission.phase,
                        is_correction=True,
                        metadata_json=json.dumps({"agent_role": "SOLUTION_ARCHITECT"})
                    )
                    db.add(new_task)
                    await db.commit()
                    
                    # Echo back to terminal
                    await manager.broadcast(mission_id, {
                        "type": "system", 
                        "message": f"[User Input Acknowledged] Appended real-time task to the {mission.phase.value if hasattr(mission.phase, 'value') else mission.phase} phase queue."
                    })

    except WebSocketDisconnect:
        manager.disconnect(websocket, mission_id)

    headers = {
        "Cache-Control": "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate",
        "Pragma": "no-cache",
        "Expires": "0",
    }
    
    valid_pages = ["features", "comparison", "dashboard", "portal"]
    if file_path in valid_pages:
        return FileResponse(f"{file_path}.html", headers=headers)
    
    if os.path.isfile(file_path):
        return FileResponse(file_path, headers=headers)
        
    return FileResponse("portal.html", headers=headers)

class RateLimiter:
    """
    Thread-safe sliding-window rate limiter.

    Tracks the number of requests per *key* (default: client IP) within a
    rolling ``window_seconds`` window.  Once a key exceeds ``max_requests``
    within the window, further calls to ``is_allowed`` return ``False`` until
    old request timestamps naturally expire out of the window.

    Attributes:
        max_requests  – maximum number of requests allowed per window.
        window_seconds – length of the sliding window in seconds.
    """

    def __init__(self, max_requests: int = 100, window_seconds: int = 60) -> None:
        if max_requests <= 0:
            raise ValueError("max_requests must be a positive integer")
        if window_seconds <= 0:
            raise ValueError("window_seconds must be a positive integer")
        self.max_requests = max_requests
        self.window_seconds = window_seconds
        # { key -> deque of Unix timestamps (float) }
        self._requests: Dict[str, Deque[float]] = defaultdict(deque)
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Public API
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def is_allowed(self, key: str) -> bool:
        """
        Return ``True`` if the *key* is still within its rate limit,
        ``False`` if it has been exceeded.

        Side-effect: registers the current request timestamp for *key*.
        """
        now = time.time()
        cutoff = now - self.window_seconds
        with self._lock:
            q = self._requests[key]
            # Evict expired timestamps from the left of the deque.
            while q and q[0] <= cutoff:
                q.popleft()
            if len(q) >= self.max_requests:
                return False
            q.append(now)
            return True

    def remaining(self, key: str) -> int:
        """Return the number of requests the *key* may still make this window."""
        now = time.time()
        cutoff = now - self.window_seconds
        with self._lock:
            q = self._requests[key]
            while q and q[0] <= cutoff:
                q.popleft()
            return max(0, self.max_requests - len(q))

    def reset(self, key: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
        """
        Clear request history.

        If *key* is given, reset only that key; otherwise reset the entire
        store (useful in tests).
        """
        with self._lock:
            if key is not None:
                self._requests.pop(key, None)
            else:
                self._requests.clear()

# ── RateLimiter unit tests ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_rate_limiter_allows_requests_within_limit() -> None:
    """Requests up to *max_requests* should all be permitted."""
    limiter = _make_test_limiter(max_requests=3)
    for _ in range(3):
        assert limiter.is_allowed("client-a") is True


def test_rate_limiter_blocks_requests_over_limit() -> None:
    """The (max_requests + 1)-th request within the window must be denied."""
    limiter = _make_test_limiter(max_requests=3)
    for _ in range(3):

    """Different keys must have independent quotas."""
    limiter = _make_test_limiter(max_requests=2)
    limiter.is_allowed("x")

    assert limiter.is_allowed("x") is False, "x should be throttled"

class RateLimiter:
    """
    Thread-safe sliding-window rate limiter.

    Tracks the number of requests per *key* (default: client IP) within a
    rolling ``window_seconds`` window.  Once a key exceeds ``max_requests``
    within the window, further calls to ``is_allowed`` return ``False`` until
    old request timestamps naturally expire out of the window.

        if max_requests <= 0:
            raise ValueError("max_requests must be a positive integer")
        if window_seconds <= 0:
            raise ValueError("window_seconds must be a positive integer")
        self.max_requests = max_requests
        self.window_seconds = window_seconds
        # { key -> deque of Unix timestamps (float) }
        self._requests: Dict[str, Deque[float]] = defaultdict(deque)
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def is_allowed(self, key: str) -> bool:
        """
        Return ``True`` if the *key* is still within its rate limit,
        ``False`` if it has been exceeded.

        Side-effect: registers the current request timestamp for *key*.
        """
        now = time.time()
        cutoff = now - self.window_seconds
        with self._lock:
            q = self._requests[key]
            # Evict expired timestamps from the left of the deque.
            while q and q[0] <= cutoff:
                q.popleft()
            if len(q) >= self.max_requests:
                return False
            q.append(now)
            return True

    def remaining(self, key: str) -> int:
        """Return the number of requests the *key* may still make this window."""
        now = time.time()
        cutoff = now - self.window_seconds
        with self._lock:
            q = self._requests[key]
            while q and q[0] <= cutoff:
                q.popleft()
            return max(0, self.max_requests - len(q))

    def reset(self, key: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
        """
        Clear request history.

        If *key* is given, reset only that key; otherwise reset the entire
        store (useful in tests).
        """
        with self._lock:
            if key is not None:
                self._requests.pop(key, None)
            else:
                self._requests.clear()

    """

class RateLimitMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
    """
    ASGI middleware that enforces per-IP rate limiting on every API route
    (paths starting with ``/api/``).  Non-API paths (static assets, WebSocket
    upgrade) are passed through untouched.

    On limit exhaustion the middleware returns HTTP **429 Too Many Requests**
    with a JSON body and the standard ``Retry-After`` header.

    Args:
        app          – The ASGI application to wrap.
        limiter      – A :class:`RateLimiter` instance.  Falls back to the
                       module-level ``_rate_limiter`` singleton if omitted.
        key_func     – Callable ``(Request) -> str`` that maps a request to its
                       rate-limit bucket.  Defaults to :func:`_get_client_key`.
        excluded_paths – Iterable of path prefixes that should bypass limiting
                         (e.g. ``["/api/health"]``).
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        app: ASGIApp,
        limiter: Optional[RateLimiter] = None,
        key_func: Optional[Callable[[Request], str]] = None,
        excluded_paths: Optional[list] = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(app)
        self._limiter = limiter or _rate_limiter
        self._key_func = key_func or _get_client_key
        self._excluded = set(excluded_paths or ["/api/health"])

    async def dispatch(
        self, request: Request, call_next: Callable[[Request], Awaitable[Response]]
    ) -> Response:
        path = request.url.path

        # Only enforce limits on /api/* routes, skip excluded paths.
        if not path.startswith("/api/") or path in self._excluded:
            return await call_next(request)

        key = self._key_func(request)
        remaining = self._limiter.remaining(key)

        if not self._limiter.is_allowed(key):
            return JSONResponse(
                status_code=429,
                content={
                    "detail": "Too Many Requests – rate limit exceeded.",
                    "limit": self._limiter.max_requests,
                    "window_seconds": self._limiter.window_seconds,
                },
                headers={
                    "Retry-After": str(self._limiter.window_seconds),
                    "X-RateLimit-Limit": str(self._limiter.max_requests),
                    "X-RateLimit-Remaining": "0",
                    "X-RateLimit-Window": str(self._limiter.window_seconds),
                },
            )

        response = await call_next(request)
        # Attach informational headers on successful responses.
        response.headers["X-RateLimit-Limit"] = str(self._limiter.max_requests)
        response.headers["X-RateLimit-Remaining"] = str(
            self._limiter.remaining(key)
        )
        response.headers["X-RateLimit-Window"] = str(self._limiter.window_seconds)
        return response
